newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita Elec says to form TV venture with BskyB.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita Elec says to form TV venture with BskyB.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Wednesday it would take part in a British digital satellite television joint venture with British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc, or BSkyB.
The Japanese electronics giant said in a statement it will form the joint venture, worth 265 million pounds, with BskyB, British Telecommunications Plc and Midland Bank SA.
Matsushita said it would take a 15 percent stake in the venture, while BSkyB and BT would each take a 32.5 percent stake and Midland Bank would hold the remaining 20 percent.
The Japanese electronics giant added that BSkyB plans to launch digital television broadcasts in the summer of 1998, eventually broadcasting on 200 channels.
Matsushita also said it would be one of the main suppliers of set-top boxes for the venture.

Matsushita said it had reached an agreement to form a joint venture called British Interactive Broadcasting Ltd (BIB) with BSkyB and the two other firms to deliver digital interactive services in Britain.
"The new company...will provide a digital platform to deliver digital interactive services to television viewers in the United Kingdom," Matsushita said in a statement.

BIB's interactive services will be made possible by the combination of digital satellite technology and telecommunications technology, making the most of the expertise of each shareholding company, Matsushita said.
It added that a new digital interactive set-top box has been developed that will allow viewers to watch BSkyB's digital satellite programming.

Viewers will also be able to receive BIB digital interactive services combining full-motion video and still pictures from satellites with still images and audio from telephone lines, the company said.

BIB's main services will include home shopping and banking as well as travel and holiday services, Matsushita said. The new company will also provide educational programming as well as games that can be downloaded, it said.
Customers will also be able to connect to an Internet service which will include e-mail capability, it said.
The service will start in the summer of 1998, subject to approval by regulatory agencies, it said.
BIB will subsidise set-top box manufacturers in order to make the retail price affordable with a view to quick market penetration, Matsushita added.
